Dramamine, stare at the horizon. Are there any other solutions?? I'm at the beach. Going on a deep sea fishing charter on Tuesday. Someone told me after your first one you kinda get used to it. Last boat excursion was at 9 or 10. I'm 30 now but do have a 9 year old (with me). So, solutions for both would be great. More so for myself because it's not my child.
How can I simply combat sea-sickness?

I have a few...stare at the horizon. Drink fizzy water or just club soda. eat some ginger before you go. As soon as I feel even a hint of seasickness, i eat something salty and crunchy (Fritos, chips)...i know that this seems a bit backwards, it really works for me...cause having an empty stomach and feeling queasy is worse for me. If you can see shore, keep your eye on a building or tree and fix on it. I live on an inlet in Florida and we are out in te ocean all the time...these things work for me.
Put some, but not too much, booze in you. And try to focus on the fishing, anything but the motion of the boat.
Raw / sugar coated ginger does wonders for sea sickness and is the only non pharmaceutical that helps from my experience.
I agree with this - I use ginger whenever I go out diving and it works without dulling my senses.

I can't stress this enough. Ginger tabs work. The folks that refused them on a recent trip we took were all vomiting. Those that took them, were laughing at those who shrugged off the value of ginger.
I also recommend drinking flat ginger ale when you're sick with the bug
They have ginger in pill form too that works very well.

If you're going to be out long enough to be eating lunch, a bit of ginger in a peanut butter and jelly sandwich is surprisingly tasty, almost-zero-effort and light enough to keep you from getting sluggish. Not that that's a great meal for when you're actually on the water, but it's good for other times you may get motion sick.

It's really worth just getting used to more ginger in your diet anyway. It's surprisingly versatile, and can play a spicy, herbal, fruity, or - if you're having an off day - soapy role in your dishes.

Dramamine is really a godsend in these situations…I didn't realize I get sea sick/motion sick until I was already on the boat for a 5 day cruise into the bahamas. Luckily the staff handed dramamine out just in case for seasick passengers, it worked wonders and I didn't get sick at all during the weeklong period.

I had water survival training when I was in the military. What our instructors told us is that you should try and concentrate on something that isn't moving. If you can see the shore look at that, but if you're out in the deep sea you should concentrate on the horizon. Also, one thing that I noticed people who got sick doing a lot was they'd get queasy and then they'd hold onto something and lock themselves into all the boat's movements. Don't do that or you'll be certain to puke. You gotta get your "sea legs". Let the deck move beneath you and just lean a little to keep your balance. Just think about it like it's a giant surfboard that you're walking around on. After a while, you won't even need to think about it.

Ugh, just reading your comment made me want to puke. Brought back memories, reminiscing on times where I was holding the rail non stop throwing up. Worse head ache ever. Honestly, it was so bad i personally wont even risk ginger with the chance of it not working. Fuucckk that, bring on the pharmaceuticals.

Stay on the center line of the ship so that when it rocks you move the least because you are the closest to the point of rotation. Look at the horizon so that you are not tricking your inner ear and eye relationship. Finally never smell diesel (if its a motor boat) and keep fresh cold wind on your face, when you start warming up you get sick much easier ( in my experience, could be anecdotal, but it also works for cars so I don't know)

Since no one else had mentioned it yet, Bonine is a good alternative to Dramamine. Some people who haven't had much luck with Dramamine have better luck with Bonine and vice versa. I'm not particularly prone to motion sickness, but my mom is, and I believe she actually prefers one for boats and the other for rollercoasters and such, though I'm not sure which way.
